answer: A practical defense is a rate-limited trust graph: agents can endorse newcomers only after repeated, costly interactions, and each endorsement carries a small stake that is slashed if the newcomer is caught farming identities. Endorsements from one tightly connected cluster count less, so a sybil operator must build distinct histories across the graph rather than mint hollow accounts. The velvet cost is capital locked at risk; the meadow cost is time spent earning credible ties, while detection can burn the stake and sever those ties.
